biological.citation: Cardiac ryanodine receptor calcium release deficiency syndrome (PMID: 33536282)
biological.summary: RyR2 loss-of-function (LOF) mutations were shown to cause a novel disease entity termed Ca2+ release deficiency syndrome (CRDS), distinct from CPVT. A RyR2 LOF mouse model exhibited cardiac electrophysiological remodeling and increased propensity for early afterdepolarizations, and a long-burst, long-pause, short-coupled pacing protocol reliably induced ventricular arrhythmias in both mice and humans with RyR2 LOF mutations. Treatment with quinidine and flecainide abolished induced arrhythmias in model mice.
biological.sample_size: Six families with linkage analysis; LOD score 11.479

biological.citation: Heart failure-induced cognitive dysfunction is mediated by intracellular Ca2+ leak through ryanodine receptor type 2 (PMID: 37429912)
biological.summary: RyR2 intracellular Ca2+ release channels were found to be expressed in hippocampal neurons of both humans and mice with heart failure, where they undergo post-translational modifications (PKA phosphorylation, oxidation, nitrosylation, calstabin2 depletion) leading to Ca2+ leak. Genetically engineered mice resistant to RyR2 Ca2+ leak (RyR2-p.Ser2808Ala) were protected against heart failure-induced cognitive dysfunction, demonstrating a role for RyR2 beyond cardiac muscle in neuronal function.

biological.citation: Hippo-Yap Signaling Maintains Sinoatrial Node Homeostasis (PMID: 36317529)
biological.summary: CUT&RUN sequencing data showed that the Hippo-Yap pathway effector Yap directly regulates Ryr2 expression in sinoatrial node (SAN) pacemaker cells. Lats1/2 conditional knockout mice showed decreased Ryr2 expression and dysregulated calcium handling in the SAN, linking RYR2 to the Hippo-Yap signaling pathway in cardiac pacemaker homeostasis.

biological.citation: Astrocyte-derived SerpinA3N promotes neuroinflammation and epileptic seizures by activating the NF-κB signaling pathway in mice with temporal lobe epilepsy (PMID: 37422673)
biological.summary: Co-immunoprecipitation experiments revealed that SerpinA3N physically interacts with RYR2 in the hippocampus of mice with kainic acid-induced temporal lobe epilepsy. SerpinA3N promotes RYR2 phosphorylation, suggesting a novel regulatory mechanism of RYR2 in neuroinflammation and seizure pathology.

biological.citation: Ero1α-Dependent ERp44 Dissociation From RyR2 Contributes to Cardiac Arrhythmia (PMID: 35086342)
biological.summary: ERp44 (endoplasmic reticulum protein 44) was identified as an intraluminal binding partner of RyR2, interacting via cysteine 4806 in a redox-sensitive manner. In a rat model of cardiac hypertrophy, Ero1α-mediated oxidation caused ERp44 dissociation from RyR2, increasing spontaneous Ca2+ release and arrhythmias; pharmacological Ero1α inhibition restored ERp44-RyR2 association and reduced arrhythmias.

biological.citation: Foxp3-mediated blockage of ryanodine receptor 2 underlies contact-based suppression by regulatory T cells (PMID: 38099494)
biological.summary: Foxp3 was shown to block transcription of RYR2 in regulatory T cells (Tregs), reducing basal Ca2+ oscillations and m-calpain activity, which prolongs DC engagement and suppresses antigen presentation. RYR2-deficient CD4+ T cells phenocopied Foxp3+ Tregs in multiple immune models (viral infection, asthma, colitis, tumor), and rescued systemic autoimmunity in scurfy mice lacking Foxp3, establishing RYR2-mediated Ca2+ signaling as a central effector mechanism of Treg immune suppression.

biological.citation: The biophysical properties of TRIC-A and TRIC-B and their interactions with RyR2 (PMID: 37756589)
biological.summary: Co-expression of mouse TRIC-A or TRIC-B with mouse RyR2 in HEK293 cells and subsequent bilayer electrophysiology demonstrated that both TRIC isoforms alter RyR2 gating behavior and its response to cytosolic Ca2+, with TRIC-A showing a greater ability to stimulate RyR2 opening. This indicates that TRIC channels directly and complementarily regulate RyR2 gating in addition to providing counter-ion currents.

biological.citation: CPVT1 point mutations in RyR2 S5 and S6 segments and their Ca2+ signaling consequence (PMID: 40974955)
biological.summary: Using CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing in human iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes, two CPVT-associated RyR2 mutations (R4822H in the S5-S6 luminal loop and L4865V on S6) were introduced and studied by TIRF imaging. R4822H completely suppressed Ca2+-induced Ca2+ release (CICR) and ICa-triggered SR Ca2+ release, while L4865V did not suppress E-C coupling but showed spontaneous Ca2+ transients, demonstrating divergent phenotypes despite both mutations being in transmembrane segments.

biological.citation: Dantrolene rescues aberrant N-terminus intersubunit interactions in mutant pro-arrhythmic cardiac ryanodine receptors (PMID: 25411383)
biological.summary: The arrhythmia-associated RyR2 L433P mutation was shown by yeast two-hybrid, co-immunoprecipitation, chemical cross-linking, and sucrose density gradient centrifugation to disrupt N-terminal self-association and impair tetramerization of the full-length channel. Dantrolene treatment restored normal N-terminal intersubunit interactions and channel function, identifying the N-terminus as a critical structural determinant for RyR2 oligomerization and a therapeutic target.

biological.citation: ASHG 2019 - Systematic whole-exome sequencing in unexplained cardiac arrest: Results from the Canadian CASPER registry and biobank (PgmNr 2657)
biological.summary: Whole-exome sequencing of 234 unexplained cardiac arrest (UCA) survivors identified a significant enrichment of rare missense RYR2 variants compared to gnomAD controls (combined allele frequency 4.1% vs. 2.0%). This supports RYR2 as a major genetic contributor to unexplained ventricular fibrillation and cardiac arrest in the absence of overt structural disease.
